description: Pull-up holding the DAC8568 CLR inactive, with a bring-up pad
notes: THE WATCHDOG IS DELETED (U-WATCHDOG, R-WDT, C-WDT all gone), so CLR has no driver and is tied INACTIVE - pulled high. A solder pad to ground beside it lets CLR be asserted BY HAND, which E7-E10 want anyway: a 99ms watchdog would have fought every 'write a code, read the meter' step of pitch calibration. Leave the DAC's clear-code register at its default so a manual CLR still parks at zero scale. Do NOT write ClearIgnore

description: Straps the DAC8568 LDAC pin to GND
notes: *** CORRECTED 2026-09-21: THIS WAS PULLED TO AVDD AND THAT GATES THE DAC. *** SBAS430E p.38 verbatim: 'For such synchronous updates, the LDAC pin is not required and it must be connected to GND permanently.' Same page: the internal LDAC register defaults to 0x00, and 'if the LDAC register bit is set to 0, the DAC channel is controlled by the LDAC pin'. So register at default + pin high = the buffer-to-DAC-register transfer is BLOCKED, and with no MISO firmware can never discover it - a module that accepts every word and moves no output. Same class as the pull-DOWN-on-CLR defect the previous redraw caught, opposite polarity, same page. | The consequence the old row claimed still holds: a hardware LDAC was considered and declined, so the six populated channels update as each word lands. BUT SBAS430E Table 11 p.36 offers 'Write to DAC input register Ch X and update all DAC registers (SW LDAC)' - five plain writes then one update-all as the last word of each pass gives a SIMULTANEOUS update in the six words already budgeted, taking the 100-200us CLR-exit window to zero for no parts and no ninth conductor

GRADE LOCKED TO C. *** THE ORDER CODE IS DAC8568ICPW, NOT DAC8568CIPW. *** DAC8568CIPW appears ZERO times in SBAS430E; its Package Option Addendum (p.54-57) enumerates DAC8568IAPW / IBPW / ICPW / IDPW and the R reel variants. The I and the grade letter were transposed, and the transposition reached ADR 0006, MANIFEST.csv and the banked file's own NAME - datasheets/analog/DAC8568CIPW.pdf is filed under a part number that does not exist. The file is correct and its SHA is correct; only the name is wrong, and renaming it would mean editing another wave's manifest fragment, which CLAUDE.md 4 forbids. Recorded here instead, per repo-maintenance.md 3 option 2: this is a fact about the PART. The grade letter selects REFERENCE GAIN as well as reset state - A/B are gain 1 (2.500V full scale), C/D are gain 2 (5.000V). An A-grade part would halve everything: pitch -2…+2.25V, mods +-5V, and channel 7 could not reach 2.500V at all. This row previously read 'DAC8568C (or A grade)' and explained the letter as reset state only. C also clears to ZERO scale where B/D clear to midscale and would park pitch octaves up. Populate 6 of 8: pitch, 4 mods, mod offset; channels 6 and 8 spare. Internal ref DISABLED by default, enable at boot. GAIN/GRADE MAPPING CONFIRMED 2026-09-21 against SBAS430E, now in the repo at datasheets/analog/DAC8568CIPW.pdf and verified verbatim: 'For device grades A and C on power-up, all DAC registers are filled with zeros and the output voltages of all DAC channels are set to zero scale.' A/B = 2.5V FSR, C/D = 5V FSR. *** TWO RIDERS THE REPO DID NOT HAVE. *** (1) THE C GRADE REQUIRES AVDD 5.0V TO 5.5V - the Electrical Characteristics table specifies grades C/D only over that range, where A/B are specified 2.7-5.5V. The LM317 nominal is 5.21V so this passes, but E7 SELECTS R-REG-SET ON THE BENCH over a 0.66V worst-case spread: a selection that lands below 5.00V puts the DAC out of spec. 5.00V is now a HARD FLOOR on that bench step, which it was not before. (2) EXTERNAL VREFIN MUST BE <= AVDD/2 ON C/D, against <= AVDD on A/B. Not binding today because the internal reference is used, but it forecloses an external-reference retrofit at anything above ~2.6V. Also from SBAS430E: reference tempco is GRADE-DEPENDENT - C/D are 2 typ / 5 max ppm/degC where A/B are 5 typ / 25 max, so the 5 ppm/degC in the pitch error budget is the C-grade MAX and is the right number. Static reference mode auto-powers the reference with the DACs; Flexible mode (DB19=1) keeps it up regardless, and BOTH default to reference OFF after any power cycle
